claims.text: A full charge-density scheme with a kinetic-energy correction can determine the presence of ferromagnetic ground states in high-entropy alloys.
The full charge-density scheme with a kinetic-energy correction is applicable to ground-state properties.
Configurational entropy is a structural mediator relevant to determining ferromagnetic ground states.
The electrical and magnetic properties of high-entropy alloys are correlated.
Configurational entropy contributes to the correlation between electrical and magnetic properties in high-entropy alloys.
The average ionic radius of the A-site cation contributes to the correlation between electrical and magnetic properties in high-entropy alloys.
Configurational entropy influences the intensity of indirect super-exchange interactions.
The average ionic radius of the A-site cation influences the intensity of indirect super-exchange interactions.
Configurational entropy and average A-site ionic radius influence the formation of ferromagnetic nanoclusters.
The method can determine whether ferromagnetic ground states are present in high-entropy alloys.
The full charge-density scheme has limitations in determining the presence of ferromagnetic ground states.
Determination of ferromagnetic ground states by this scheme is uncertain.
Ab initio calculations can be used to test the proposed determination method.
Failure of the scheme to predict a ferromagnetic ground state would falsify the hypothesis.
